candidate.title: AmpliSeq™ for Illumina
candidate.scope: The supplied Illumina product-preparation schematic for AmpliSeq™ for Illumina, from alternative DNA or RNA inputs to indexed DNA library product ready for cluster generation. RNA alone first undergoes reverse transcription. The common drawn DNA/cDNA route is instantiated separately below for each input provenance; these are alternative uses of one schematic, not two named methods, pooling, or a claim that both substrates are processed together. The scope ends before cluster generation or sequencing and does not establish a complete single-cell assay.

states.label: DNA input / DNA template
features: Supplied DNA is shown as two blue parallel strands at the upper left and enters the DNA/cDNA template boundary directly.
At the shared template boundary, short opposed magenta and cyan primer marks delimit a region of the longer DNA.
This route does not require the depicted RNA reverse-transcription step.

evidence.locator: Upper input alternatives: double-line DNA at left; 5′–3′ RNA at right; arrows to DNA/cDNA
DNA/cDNA boundary: long blue double line with opposed short magenta and cyan primer marks

states.label: RNA input
features: Purple single strand labelled RNA, with 5′ at the left and 3′ at the right.
Alternative biological starting material to the upper-left DNA input.

evidence.locator: Upper input alternatives: double-line DNA at left; 5′–3′ RNA at right; arrows to DNA/cDNA

states.label: RNA-derived cDNA template
features: DNA product of the Reverse transcribe step, entering the common DNA/cDNA boundary.
The common boundary uses a blue double-line representation with opposed colored primer marks; separate second-strand synthesis is not depicted.
The downstream DNA insert therefore represents sequence copied from the RNA input.

DNA/cDNA boundary: long blue double line with opposed short magenta and cyan primer marks

states.label: Primer-trimmed target amplicon from supplied DNA

states.label: Adaptor-ligated amplicon from supplied DNA

evidence.locator: Ligate adaptors: arrow from trimmed duplex to blue duplex bearing green left and magenta right adaptor segments

states.label: Adaptor-bearing target with added primer constructs from supplied DNA
features: Central blue insert is shown with end-associated primer constructs.
At the left of this intermediate, the green adaptor-associated construct has a slanted tail labelled Index 1 and P7.
At the right, the magenta adaptor-associated construct has a slanted tail labelled Index 2 and P5.
This intermediate depicts added primers; the following PCR produces the completed linear indexed product.

states.label: Indexed library product from supplied DNA, ready for cluster generation

operations.label: Reverse transcribe
operations.description: Convert the RNA input into a cDNA template for the subsequent DNA amplification route. The figure joins this alternative route to the DNA/cDNA boundary; it does not depict mixing RNA-derived cDNA with the direct DNA input.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription, as explicitly labelled; no additional cDNA synthesis chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: Changes the carrier from RNA to DNA while retaining a sequence representation of the RNA template.

evidence.locator: Upper right RNA input and downward arrow labelled Reverse transcribe, ending at DNA/cDNA

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the region delimited by the opposed primer marks in the supplied DNA template. The output is a shorter DNA amplicon containing the target-derived central segment and the depicted primer-derived ends.
operations.mechanism: PCR, explicitly labelled in the figure.
operations.information_effect: The central insert carries an amplified sequence representation of the selected region of supplied DNA; the figure does not show genome-wide or transcriptome-wide sampling.

evidence.locator: First PCR: downward arrow from DNA/cDNA to a shorter blue duplex with magenta left and cyan right ends

operations.label: Remove primer sequences
operations.description: Trim the primer-derived terminal regions of the first PCR amplicon while retaining its target-derived central DNA. The drawing still shows small colored terminal tips, so it does not establish removal of every primer-derived nucleotide.
operations.information_effect: Retains the target-derived DNA carrier while reducing the represented primer-derived flanks.

evidence.locator: Remove primer sequences: arrow from first amplicon to shorter duplex with small residual magenta/cyan tips

operations.label: Ligate adaptors
operations.description: Attach the depicted green and magenta adaptors to opposite ends of the primer-trimmed DNA amplicon, producing an adaptor-flanked target insert.
operations.mechanism: Adaptor ligation, explicitly labelled; adaptor sequences, enzyme identity and end-group chemistry are unspecified.
operations.information_effect: Adds end interfaces while retaining the central target-derived sequence.

evidence.locator: Ligate adaptors: arrow from trimmed duplex to blue duplex bearing green left and magenta right adaptor segments

operations.label: Add sequencing primers
operations.description: Add the depicted end-associated primer constructs to the adaptor-bearing amplicon. The constructs introduce the shown Index 1/P7 and Index 2/P5 tails at opposite ends, before the final PCR.
operations.information_effect: Places index and P5/P7 sequence information at the target insert ends for incorporation into the final DNA library. The diagram supplies no index sequences or sample/cell assignment scheme.

evidence.locator: Add sequencing primers: arrow from adaptor-ligated duplex to end-associated tailed primer constructs labelled P7, Index 1, Index 2 and P5

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the primer-associated adaptor-bearing target so that the index-bearing and P5/P7 terminal constructs are represented in the completed linear DNA library product. This is the second PCR in the schematic, after adaptor ligation and primer addition.
operations.mechanism: PCR, explicitly labelled in the figure.
operations.information_effect: The final readout carrier is DNA containing a selected sequence from supplied DNA, physically linked to Index 2/P5 and Index 1/P7 end segments. Later sequencing could identify represented insert sequence and its index tags. The figure itself supplies no sequence reads, abundance calibration, or per-cell identity.

evidence.locator: Second PCR: downward arrow from tailed primer constructs to Product ready for cluster generation; final end labels P5–Index 2 and Index 1–P7
Bottom indexed target-insert product and Product ready for cluster generation label
evidence.rationale: The blue target-derived insert remains connected to the labelled index and P5/P7 end segments in the final product. Thus later sequencing can interrogate the represented insert with its attached index sequences; neither sequencing itself nor a quantitative or cell-identity readout is drawn.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and diagram name one target: AmpliSeq™ for Illumina. The top DNA and RNA drawings are alternative input routes within that target. op_rt applies only to RNA. Operations with the dna prefix instantiate the drawn downstream captions for supplied DNA; operations with the rna prefix instantiate the same captions for cDNA produced by op_rt. Duplicating these local instances preserves preparation history and does not assert two physical workflows run jointly. No pooling is drawn. The method association is supported at schematic scope by the title and pictured route; the card supplies no primary-paper references or historical/version claim.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete schematic-level architecture: DNA enters directly, RNA becomes cDNA, and each alternative proceeds through target PCR, primer-sequence removal, adaptor ligation, addition of the depicted tailed primers, and final PCR to indexed DNA ready for cluster generation. All 13 states, 11 local operations, and 22 material routes were checked against the image and against their interfaces. Every depicted transformation and both input alternatives are retained; no multi-input operation, pooling, compartment change, unshown chemistry, or cell-identity readout is asserted. The two PCR instances are distinct, and DNA/RNA provenance remains separate. P5–Index 2 and P7–Index 1 associations persist despite the final drawing reversing left/right orientation. The single-line endpoint does not establish single-stranded chemistry. No supplied paper or consequential source conflict requires a correction or research; this acceptance does not verify a full laboratory implementation.
